faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, so the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, super, and any salary sacrifice arrangements.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the simplest way to compare them is to convert one to the other. The standard formula in Australia is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For full-time employees, we assume a 38-hour week (the ordinary hours defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman). That means you multiply your hourly rate by 1,976 (38 × 52). For example, if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross pay is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280.

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply double your weekly pay. Using the example above, weekly pay is $30 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280. This can help you match your pay cycle to your expenses.

## Key Pay Rates and What They Mean

Australia has several pay benchmarks. It is important to distinguish between them:

- **National Minimum Wage**: Set by the Fair Work Commission, currently $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) for a 38-hour week. This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement.
- **Award rates**: Many industries have specific awards that set minimum pay rates higher than the National Minimum Wage. These rates vary by job classification and experience. Check the relevant award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or use our [pay guides](/blog) to find your rate.
- **Casual loading**: Casual employees receive an extra 25% on top of their base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. The casual minimum wage is $33.05 per hour. When using our [the timesheet](/), you can check a box to add the 25% loading to your base hourly rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading.
- **Average earnings**: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) for full-time adult ordinary time as $2,083.70 per week. This is an average across all industries and states, not a median for any specific job. All employees (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week.

If you are looking for a specific occupation, remember that industry or state averages are not the same as a job median. Our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) reference can help you find relevant data, but we do not invent precise figures for individual roles.

## Tax, Super, and Salary Sacrifice

Once you have your gross annual pay, you need to consider tax and superannuation.

### Income Tax (2026–27 Resident Rates)

The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale. For 2026–27:
- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy of 2% applies to most residents (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). This is an estimate; your actual tax may differ if you have HELP debt, the Medicare levy surcharge, or other adjustments.

### Super Guarantee

Your employer must pay superannuation on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. For example, if your gross annual pay is $80,000, your employer adds $9,600 to your super fund (12% of $80,000), provided you are under the cap.

### Salary Sacrifice: How Does It Work?

Salary sacrifice is an arrangement where you agree to forgo part of your before-tax salary in exchange for benefits such as additional super contributions, a car, or electronic devices. This reduces your taxable income, so you pay less income tax. However, it also reduces your ordinary earnings, which may lower the super guarantee your employer pays (since it is calculated on your reduced ordinary earnings). The Australian Taxation Office sets rules on what can be sacrificed and any fringe benefits tax implications.

For example, if you earn $90,000 and salary sacrifice $10,000 into super, your taxable income drops to $80,000. You pay less tax, but your employer's super guarantee is now based on $80,000 (12% = $9,600) instead of $90,000 (12% = $10,800). The net effect depends on your marginal tax rate and the type of benefit. Always consult a tax professional or use our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) reference for more details.

## Using Our Tools

Our [the timesheet](/), the home page, lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates your annual gross pay, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, and super. The results assume a 38-hour week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For more detailed estimates, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

If you need to check award rates or industry averages, visit our [reference tables](/data) or [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. For converting between hourly and annual rates, the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) topic has additional examples.

## Important Disclaimer

This article provides an estimate only. Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings paid on top, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold, and Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is not a determination of your actual pay or tax liability.
